page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at up to 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports standard x86 extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but does not provide AVX-512 extensions.

Hardware resource allocation is characterized by an elevated memory-to-core ratio, delivering 64.0 GB of system memory, which equals 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring external Azure managed storage for non-volatile data persistence and operating system operations.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching 2,701.19 on the stress-ng single-core test. Conversely, parallel execution capability is constrained by the 4-vCPU ceiling, yielding lower relative multi-core scores in stress-ng (5,398.78) and Geekbench (3,636.0). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 39.23 GB/sec for reads and 22.78 GB/sec for writes. In-memory data store performance includes 4.13 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core layout of the E8-4as_v5 offers substantial memory density without requiring payment for an 8-core allocation. This architecture makes the instance effective for database caching tiers, in-memory key-value stores, intermediate ETL buffering, and memory-constrained enterprise software licensing models.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX and AES instructions, though AVX-512 is absent. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware, depending entirely on network-attached storage volumes for disk operations. Benchmark metrics reflect top-quartile single-core CPU execution, while total multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect the lower core count. By offering an expanded memory footprint on a constrained core setup, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data transformation pipelines.
